'''Paul Anthony Madden''' (born 10 October 1948<ref>[https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/officers/aMyb1S14b3VGsFc_zEr7goJiaNs/appointments Companies House]</ref>) is a British [[chemist]] and former [[List of Provosts of The Queen's College, Oxford|Provost of The Queen's College, Oxford]].

==Early life==
Madden attended [[St Bede's Grammar School]], a Catholic boys' [[grammar school]] in [[Bradford]], Yorkshire, England. He gained BSc and DPhil degrees in chemistry at the [[University of Sussex]].<ref name="WW 2019">{{cite web |title=Madden, Prof. Paul Anthony |url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-43916 |website=[[Who's Who 2019]] |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=2 August 2019 |language=en |doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U43916 |date=1 December 2018|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4 }}</ref> His doctoral thesis was titled "Reactive Scattering Calculations" and was completed in 1974.<ref name="thesis">{{cite web |last1=Madden |first1=P. A. |title=Reactive Scattering Calculations |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.464570 |website=E-Thesis Online Service |publisher=The British Library Board |access-date=2 August 2019 |date=1974}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1981 to 1984 he worked at the [[Royal Signals and Radar Establishment]] in [[Malvern, Worcestershire]].

From 1984 until 2005 he was [[Fellow#Oxford, Cambridge and Dublin|Fellow]] in Chemistry at [[The Queen's College, Oxford]] and also Senior Tutor of the college and Chairman of the University Information Technology Committee. From 2004<ref>[http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/college-news/New%20Provost The Queen's College, Oxford: College News] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080913205342/http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/college-news/New%20Provost |date=13 September 2008 }}</ref> until 2008 he was Professor of Physical Chemistry and Director of Centre for Science at Extreme Conditions at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref>[http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/appeals/brochures/chemistry_appeal.pdf The Queen's College Chemistry Appeal] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070812222154/http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/appeals/brochures/chemistry_appeal.pdf |date=12 August 2007 }}</ref> He took up the office of [[Provost (education)|Provost]] of [[The Queen's College, Oxford|The Queen's College]] on 2 August 2008 and was succeeded by Dr [[Claire Craig]] CBE on 2 August 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/college-news/pre-election-of-51st-provost|title= Pre-election of 51st Provost|access-date=2008-07-21 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080622164152/http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/college-news/pre-election-of-51st-provost <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 2008-06-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/news/queens-college-announces-provost-pre-election|title=The Queen's College announces pre-election of its next Provost|access-date=19 October 2018|publisher=The Queen's College}}</ref>

He was awarded the Mulliken Medal of the University of Chicago for his achievements in Theoretical and Physical Chemistry.<ref>[http://physchem.ox.ac.uk/pdf/annrep02.pdf ''Report of Dr. Lee's Professor of Chemistry for the Year Ended 31st July 2002'']</ref> He has served as Miller Visiting Professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>[http://physchem.ox.ac.uk/annual_report/annrep04.html ''Report of Dr. Lee's Professor of Chemistry for the Year Ended 31st July 2004'']</ref> 
He was elected to the [[Royal Society|Fellowship of the Royal Society]] in 2001 and is a [[Royal Society of Edinburgh|Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]].

He was appointed a member of the ''ad hoc'' Board of Electors to the Professorship of Chemistry in the University of Cambridge on the nomination of the Faculty Board of Chemistry.<ref>[http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2006-07/weekly/6063/5.html ''Cambridge University Reporter'' 7 February 2007]</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married to Alison.
